subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**urgent**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence discusses how Ms. Navalnaya acted quickly to get her husband out of Russia after he was poisoned — a life-threatening emergency.
 
• The adjective "**urgent**" is appropriate as it refers to something requiring immediate action or attention, especially in medical contexts. (आपातकालीन)
 
• The phrase "**urgent treatment**" correctly conveys the seriousness of the situation involving a nerve agent.
 
• Other options do not fit the context:
 
 
• **Slow** – Opposite of the urgency implied.
 
• **Crazy** – Informal, inappropriate for a formal and serious context.
 
• **Interesting** – Not relevant to medical emergency or treatment.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of her husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for **urgent**__ treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Slow** – (धीमा): Does not convey the seriousness of a medical emergency.

 **Example:** The recovery process was slow and steady.
 
• **Crazy** – (पागलपन भरा): Informal and emotionally charged, not suitable for describing treatment.

 **Example:** It was a crazy idea to hike in that weather.
 
• **Interesting** – (दिलचस्प): Describes something engaging or curious, not appropriate for emergency treatment.

 **Example:** She told an interesting story.
